1. Employee.java (Abstract Base Class)
Java
package org.howard.edu.lsp.midterm.inheritance;

/**
 * Represents a generic employee in the system.
 * Serves as the base class for specific employee types.
 */
public abstract class Employee {
    private double hoursWorked;
    private double hourlyRate;

    /**
     * Constructs an Employee with the specified hours worked and hourly rate.
     *
     * @param hoursWorked the number of hours the employee worked
     * @param hourlyRate  the hourly pay rate for the employee
     */
    public Employee(double hoursWorked, double hourlyRate) {
        this.hoursWorked = hoursWorked;
        this.hourlyRate = hourlyRate;
    }

    /**
     * Gets the number of hours worked.
     *
     * @return the hours worked
     */
    public double getHoursWorked() {
        return hoursWorked;
    }

    /**
     * Gets the hourly rate of pay.
     *
     * @return the hourly rate
     */
    public double getHourlyRate() {
        return hourlyRate;
    }

    /**
     * Calculates the pay for the employee.
     * This method must be implemented by all subclasses.
     *
     * @return the calculated pay
     */
    public abstract double calculatePay();
}
2. FullTimeEmployee.java
Java
package org.howard.edu.lsp.midterm.inheritance;

/**
 * Represents a full-time employee who is eligible for overtime pay.
 */
public class FullTimeEmployee extends Employee {

    /**
     * Constructs a FullTimeEmployee with the specified hours and rate.
     *
     * @param hoursWorked the number of hours worked
     * @param hourlyRate  the base hourly rate
     */
    public FullTimeEmployee(double hoursWorked, double hourlyRate) {
        super(hoursWorked, hourlyRate);
    }

    /**
     * Calculates pay for a full-time employee.
     * Hours up to 40 are paid at the base rate. Hours over 40 are paid at 1.5x the base rate.
     *
     * @return the total calculated pay including overtime
     */
    @Override
    public double calculatePay() {
        double hours = getHoursWorked();
        double rate = getHourlyRate();
        
        if (hours > 40) {
            double regularPay = 40 * rate;
            double overtimePay = (hours - 40) * (rate * 1.5);
            return regularPay + overtimePay;
        } else {
            return hours * rate;
        }
    }
}
3. PartTimeEmployee.java
Java
package org.howard.edu.lsp.midterm.inheritance;

/**
 * Represents a part-time employee who receives straight pay with no overtime.
 */
public class PartTimeEmployee extends Employee {

    /**
     * Constructs a PartTimeEmployee with the specified hours and rate.
     *
     * @param hoursWorked the number of hours worked
     * @param hourlyRate  the base hourly rate
     */
    public PartTimeEmployee(double hoursWorked, double hourlyRate) {
        super(hoursWorked, hourlyRate);
    }

    /**
     * Calculates pay for a part-time employee.
     * Part-time employees receive their standard hourly rate for all hours worked.
     *
     * @return the total calculated pay
     */
    @Override
    public double calculatePay() {
        return getHoursWorked() * getHourlyRate();
    }
}
4. Contractor.java
Java
package org.howard.edu.lsp.midterm.inheritance;

/**
 * Represents a contractor who receives a premium rate on all hours worked.
 */
public class Contractor extends Employee {

    /**
     * Constructs a Contractor with the specified hours and base rate.
     *
     * @param hoursWorked the number of hours worked
     * @param hourlyRate  the base hourly rate before the premium is applied
     */
    public Contractor(double hoursWorked, double hourlyRate) {
        super(hoursWorked, hourlyRate);
    }

    /**
     * Calculates pay for a contractor.
     * Contractors receive a 15% premium (1.15 multiplier) on their hourly rate.
     *
     * @return the total calculated pay including the premium
     */
    @Override
    public double calculatePay() {
        return getHoursWorked() * getHourlyRate() * 1.15;
    }
}
How and Why It Works
Inheritance: We created an abstract base class Employee that holds the common fields (hoursWorked, hourlyRate) and an abstract method calculatePay(). FullTimeEmployee, PartTimeEmployee, and Contractor all inherit from this base class.

Method Overriding: Instead of one massive if/else block trying to juggle every rule, each subclass overrides the calculatePay() method to provide its own specific mathematical logic.

Polymorphism in Action: In the provided Driver.java, look at the test() method signature: private static void test(String label, Employee employee, double expected). The driver can pass any subclass (like a FullTimeEmployee or a Contractor) into the employee parameter. When the driver calls employee.calculatePay(), Java automatically knows at runtime which specific version of the calculation to run based on the actual object type. This eliminates the need for string comparisons like employeeType.equals("FULL_TIME").
